title: [still present since r3] W4's check_manifest_prefix misaligns stepped-tick hashes against the wall-window manifest — motion-strip falsely refuses valid strips on paused demos (reproduced, exit 2)
detail: The W4 fix collects hashes only for stepped ticks but compares them positionally against the blessed manifest, which run_demo indexes per wall window (paused windows included). Any strip window that steps ticks after a pause falsely reports divergence and aborts.
recommended_fix: Index-align: build the strip's hash array per wall window (append the stable-state hash for paused windows, like run_demo), or track the wall-window index per stepped tick and compare manifest[wall_tick-1]. Verify with `motion-strip pause 71000 72000 100`.

title: [still present since r3] W3 half-fixed: interp_continuous now reads p.delivered, but the delivery pin STILL passes via anchor mismatch — deleting the delivered guard breaks no test
detail: Production semantics are fixed (the flag is read), but the pin remains vacuous for the delivered path: a regression deleting `if p.delivered { return false }` passes all 33 render tests and every gate silently.
recommended_fix: Make the anchor CONTINUOUS so only the flag decides: set p.at_node = 1 == entry_heading (arrival-shaped) with p.delivered = true, assert false; keep a companion assert that the same packet with delivered=false is continuous.

title: motion_strip.odin header still claims "T1 manifest + replay gate are NOT re-verified here" — contradicts the W4 check_manifest_prefix call added in the same commit; plus an orphaned usage-comment fragment
detail: The file-header documentation contradicts the code it precedes: a reader trusting the header would believe the strip has no T1 net. The dangling fragment is leftover from the r3 N9 comment edit.
recommended_fix: Update the header to state the manifest PREFIX is verified per stepped tick; delete the orphaned "the golden path (…)" continuation line.

title: interp_continuous's doc comment is physically attached to interp_alpha_from_accum — the r4 helper was inserted mid-comment (view.odin:135-166)
evidence: Line 135: "// interp_continuous — may the render lerp between the row's anchor (the" … the comment runs continuously into line 143: "// interp_alpha_from_accum — the ONE interpolation-activation derivation" with no blank line, then line 153 defines "interp_alpha_from_accum :: proc(running: bool, accum, tick_seconds: f64) -> f32 {" and only line 166 defines "interp_continuous :: proc(".
detail: The activation helper was spliced between interp_continuous's doc comment and its definition, so the lerp-semantics doc precedes the wrong proc. Confusing for future readers; doc-tooling would bind it to interp_alpha_from_accum.
recommended_fix: Move the interp_alpha_from_accum definition+comment below interp_continuous (or above the comment block) so each proc owns its doc.

title: check_manifest_prefix duplicates check_manifest's ~28-line header block verbatim and silently drops the manifest-corrupt check (ticks header vs hash-line count)
evidence:
check_manifest lines 113-125 and check_manifest_prefix lines 155-167 are line-for-line identical (version/seed/catalog_hash/logic_hz checks). check_manifest additionally has:
	if m.ticks != i64(len(m.hashes)) {
		append(fails, fmt.tprintf("T1: manifest corrupt — ticks header %d but %d hash lines",
			m.ticks, len(m.hashes)))
		ok = false
	}
check_manifest_prefix has no equivalent, so a corrupt manifest passes the strip's net.
detail: Two copies of the header-drift logic must now be edited in lockstep; the prefix variant also omits the corrupt-manifest guard run_demo's checker carries.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared check_manifest_header(m, demo, catalog_hash, logic_hz, fails) helper called by both; include the ticks-vs-hashes guard in it.
